_comment: The on-screen paddle keyer (#233), pinned for both ports:
Each case is a script of paddle presses and releases fed to a fresh keyer
in time order, then the clock run on to `untilMs`. `expected` gives, per
keyer mode, every element the keyer sends as [element, keyDownMs, keyUpMs].
Every expected value was worked out by hand from the rules in
`derivation`, not captured from either port, so both ports drifting the

derivation.timing: One unit is 1200 / wpm ms (PARIS). A dit keys down for 1 unit, a dah for 3. Every element is followed by 1 unit of silence; the element plus that silence is its slot. The keyer is busy for the whole slot and decides what comes next at the slot's end.
derivation.idle: A paddle pressed while the keyer is idle starts its own element at the moment of the press.
derivation.memory: A paddle pressed while the keyer is busy (anywhere in the slot, tone or silence) is latched. Starting an element clears that element's latch. Holding a paddle is not a press; only the down edge latches.
derivation.iambic: Iambic A and B, at a slot's end: if the opposite of the element just sent is held or latched, send the opposite; otherwise, if the same element is held or latched, send it again; otherwise go idle. Squeezing both therefore alternates.
derivation.modeB: Iambic B also latches the opposite paddle if it is already held when an element starts. So releasing a squeeze sends one more alternate element after the one in progress; mode A stops after the element in progress.
derivation.ultimatic: Ultimatic, at a slot's end: if both paddles are held or latched, send the element of the one pressed most recently; if one is, send its element; otherwise go idle. Squeezing repeats the last-pressed paddle's element instead of alternating.
derivation.ties: A slot or tone ending at the same instant as a paddle event is processed first; the event is applied after it.

cases.name: a held dit repeats until released
a held dah repeats until released
squeeze dit first, both released during the third element
dit memory: a dit tapped during a dah is sent after it
dah memory: a dah tapped during a dit is sent after it
squeeze dah first, both released during the dit
a long squeeze, both released during the fourth element
releasing the second paddle of a squeeze hands back to the first
a dit tapped into a held dah
30 WPM: a held dah, then a dit from idle
a release at the very instant a slot ends comes after the decision
